items.title: ‘He could’ve been saved’: Minor’s body found 3 days after he fell in Delhi drain chasing a kite
items.summary: A JCB excavator pulled Mithun’s body out of an open drain in Southeast Delhi’s Jasola village at around 1.15 pm on Tuesday. He was 15. He had slipped into that drain on Saturday morning, chasing a kite thread a few steps from his house. The body has now been shifted to AIIMS Delhi, police sources said. Mithun’s mother Anita Devi says her son “could have been saved”. “If the police had begun the search operation on Saturday itself then maybe it wouldn’t have reached this point,” she alleged. For much of the three days in between, Mithun’s father says he searched for it himself. Awadesh cleans sewers for a living and has lived in Jasola for nearly 18 years. A video of him wading through the water, looking for his son, went viral on Monday. The recovery closes a search that Mithun’s family claims never seriously began. Over three days they claim to have watched five agencies – Delhi Police, the Delhi Fire Service, the Delhi Disaster Management Authority, the National Disaster Response Force and the Boat Club – arrive at the drain and, in their account, manage to do little. One junior engineer has been suspended. The family says that is worth nothing to them. The search Mithun’s mother

items.title: Ajeet Bharti moves Delhi court for anticipatory bail, says no case made out under SC/ST Act
items.summary: YouTuber and commentator Ajeet Bharti has approached Delhi's Patiala House Court seeking anticipatory bail in the case registered against him under the Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe (Prevention of Atrocities) Act (SC/ST Act). The case was heard today by Additional Sessions Judge (ASJ) Saurabh Pratap Singh Laler . Advocate Jai Anant Dehadrai and Pratyush Prasanna appeared for Bharti and argued that no offence under the SC/ST Act was made out against him on the facts of this case. Dehadrai added that the police was yet to issue a notice under Section 35(3) of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) to Bharti. Section 35(3) mandates that police officers must issue a written notice of appearance to an accused person in cases where an immediate arrest is not required. After hearing the case briefly, the Court said that if the police issues a notice to Bharti, the same must be placed before the Court for examination. "In the event such notice is issued by the Investigating Officer, a copy thereof shall be placed by IO on record of this Court, so that the Court may examine the date of issuance of the notice and the prima facie satisfaction regarding the ingredients of the offence

items.title: Supreme Court directs Tarun Tejpal to surrender within 3 weeks
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Tuesday directed former Tehelka editor Tarun Tejpal, convicted in rape case, to surrender before jail authorities within three weeks. The Court rejected Tejpal's application for exemption from surrendering, and said it will start hearing Tejpal's appeal against his conviction by the High Court only after he surrenders and files a surrender certificate. Justice Alok Aradhe on Tuesday asked Tejpal's counsel how much time he would require to surrender. Senior Advocate Kapil Sibal , appearing for Tejpal, said he would need two weeks. The Court then proceeded to record the same and posted the case for hearing on September 22 subject to Tejpal filing a surrender certificate by that date. "Appellant shall surrender within a period of 3 weeks and file his surrender certificate. In case the surrender certificate is filed on or before September 22, the office is directed to list the matter in court on September 22," the Court stated in its order.
